answer: In an agent marketplace buying pigment for a jetty repair, each bidding identity must lock $100 in escrow for 30 days. Buyers weight bids by locked stake, so reputation is a costly signal rather than a count of names. An attacker can create a thousand agents, but must immobilize $100,000 to give them full weight; splitting one deposit among aliases adds no influence because voting power follows total escrowed dollars.
